candidates.title: Open-carton rejection by sidewall body pinch
candidates.objective: On a running friction-driven belt, detect an open carton, avoid its collision-enabled flaps, pinch the body below the hinges, and place the carton and all free contents in a reject tray; leave initially closed cartons untouched to cross the downstream line.
candidates.success_conditions: Per open carton: 0.25 for opposed pad contacts within the z=15–40 mm body band; 0.50 after the complete carton clears the belt by at least 20 mm with every content item retained; 0.75 when carton and contents are inside the tray; 1.00 after complete release, at least 60 mm robot clearance, and 3.0 s stable dwell from fresh 10 Hz observations. A content item leaving the carton and touching anything outside its interior permanently caps that carton at 0.50; a dropped carton scores 0. Initially closed cartons score 1.00 only after untouched passage along the original belt path. Full score requires every reject removed and every closed carton passed. Physics validation uses separately labeled 240 Hz traces and is not a grading condition.
candidates.industrial_value: Cartoners detect and reject open-flap cartons, while spill-prone open packages can be unsuitable for forceful rejection. The proposed robotic pinch is a representative careful-removal method, not a claimed manufacturer procedure.
candidates.dexterity: High: synchronize with a translating carton, approach a 25 mm-high body contact band beneath moving finite-thickness flaps, establish bilateral contact, lift nearly level, preserve loose contents, and release cleanly.

candidates.asset_plan: Use pinned Isaac Sim 6.1.0.0 and YAM commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730. Start with a representative 120×70×70 mm external carton, 2 mm rigid compound walls, four 2 mm collision-enabled hinged flaps, a proposed z=15–40 mm contact band, and three free 18 mm rigid contents. The pinned constants describe a nominal 94 mm open pad separation; the 24 mm difference from carton width is not measured clearance. Validate finger, palm, belt, and flap swept-volume clearance natively. Use frictional surface motion only. Gate work through stationary grasp/lift, stationary transfer and release, moving open carton, untouched closed-carton passage, then mixed stream. Model closed-flap retention explicitly and disclose its calibrated break-free threshold as a testable assumption.
candidates.risk: The corrected geometry is internally consistent, but no native physical grasp trace exists. Novelty fails if flap interference and spill preservation do not measurably distinguish the task from generic conveyor selection and pick-and-place. Corrugated compliance is simplified as rigid walls.
missing_evidence: Independent visual verification of the relevant FEFCO and Rovema diagrams; acquired PDFs exist, but this read-only run could not render their pages for inspection
Pinned-YAM physical trace confirming pad and palm clearance around the 70 mm carton and z=15–40 mm contact band
Validated closed-flap retention threshold and hinge/contact parameters

candidates.title: Bimanual end-wall cradle rejection
candidates.objective: Track an open carton and support its two short body walls with separate grippers below the flap hinges, then coordinate a level lift and tray placement without losing free contents; leave closed cartons untouched.
candidates.success_conditions: Per open carton: 0.25 for simultaneous support on opposite short body walls below the hinges; 0.50 for at least 20 mm complete belt clearance with all contents retained; 0.75 for carton and contents inside the tray; 1.00 after both grippers release, remain at least 60 mm clear, and the result stays stable for 3.0 s. Apply the same permanent spill cap, drop loss, closed-carton no-contact condition, and downstream passage rule as the sidewall candidate. Hand assignment and contact order are irrelevant.
candidates.industrial_value: This evaluates careful removal after a documented open-flap reject decision where a forceful reject could spill contents. Bimanual cradling is proposed test geometry, not an asserted factory procedure.
candidates.dexterity: Very high: both arms must match belt motion, avoid four articulated flaps, share load without yawing or crushing the carton, and clear one another during release.

candidates.asset_plan: Reuse the corrected 120×70×70 mm rigid carton and free contents, but expose both short-wall approaches. Validate stationary simultaneous access, arm-arm clearance, opposing support, load sharing, lift attitude, and coordinated release before enabling belt motion.
candidates.risk: No acquired procedure establishes bimanual cradling, and simultaneous access is substantially more demanding than the single-gripper option.
missing_evidence: Pinned-YAM trace demonstrating collision-free simultaneous end-wall access
Contact and body traces demonstrating a level lift without grasp welding
Release-clearance trace covering both arms, flaps, carton, and tray

candidates.title: Flap stabilization with body extraction
candidates.objective: When an open flap obstructs the body approach, control that articulated flap with one gripper while the other acquires a body-wall grasp and transfers the carton to the reject tray without spilling; leave closed cartons untouched.
candidates.success_conditions: Per open carton: 0.25 when the obstructing flap is controlled without damage or conversion to a closed state; 0.50 when a valid body grasp lifts the whole carton at least 20 mm with every content item retained; 0.75 when carton and contents are inside the tray; 1.00 after complete release, 60 mm robot clearance, and 3.0 s stability. Flap-only lifting cannot exceed 0.25. Spill permanently caps the carton at 0.50; a drop or any robot contact with a closed carton scores that carton 0. Equivalent safe flap-control methods are accepted regardless of hand identity or order.
candidates.industrial_value: The task makes an actual open flap an active collision constraint during documented defect rejection, rather than a visual label. The stabilization strategy itself is not claimed as standard industrial practice.
candidates.dexterity: Extreme: one arm controls a translating articulated obstacle while the other establishes a body grasp, followed by coordinated lift and collision-free withdrawal.

candidates.asset_plan: Use the corrected 120×70×70 mm carton but configure one finite-thickness flap to obstruct part of an otherwise reachable body approach. Author explicit hinge limits, damping, mass, and collision thickness. Validate free hinge behavior, stationary flap control, simultaneous body grasp, and safe release before adding belt motion.
candidates.risk: This variant risks forcing an artificial strategy. The flap must physically impede generic grasping without making stabilization the only arbitrarily prescribed solution.
missing_evidence: Industrial procedure or video supporting flap stabilization during removal, or evidence that this representative mechanism preserves the real skill without claiming standard practice
Validated hinge and contact parameters producing realistic obstruction
Pinned-YAM trace of simultaneous flap control and body grasp

selection_reason: No candidate can be selected under the requirement that selection is limited to ready candidates with no critical missing evidence. The sidewall-pinch candidate is the preferred first build and corrects the prior 110 mm-height, 80 mm-band, and alleged measured-clearance errors, but independent diagram inspection and native YAM clearance/contact validation remain unavailable. Marking it ready would repeat the prior failure by asserting construction readiness without the required evidence.
